title: Fixed amount vs percentage
objectives: Compare a fixed-amount step-up with a percentage step-up.
Say which suits a client with an irregular income.
body_md:
There are two ways to set a step-up, and the difference compounds.

## Fixed amount

Adds the same rupee amount each time: ₹10,000 → ₹11,000 → ₹12,000 → ₹13,000. It is gentler and easier to budget.

## Percentage

Raises the instalment by a set share of the previous one. At 10%: ₹10,000 → ₹11,000 → ₹12,100 → ₹13,310.

## Why the percentage grows faster

Every raise is applied to a bigger base. The fixed amount adds ₹1,000 every year; the percentage adds 10% of an amount that is itself growing. Over 20 years the difference is large.

## Which to choose

- Fixed amount: irregular income, a tight budget, a client who wants a number they can predict.
- Percentage: salaried income growing every year, and a goal that is still far away.

Both are valid. The best one is the one the client will not cancel in a tight month.
example: At ₹10,000 a month, a fixed +₹1,000 reaches ₹14,000 by year 5; a 10% step-up reaches ₹14,641. By year 20 the gap is far wider, because one is linear and the other compounds.
say: A fixed step-up adds the same rupees each year; a percentage adds a share of a growing amount.
A percentage step-up grows faster because each raise is on a bigger base.
never: A percentage step-up is always better.
A fixed step-up never catches up.
